answer: Merge identities whose online sessions rise and fall together. Real agents run on separate machines for separate owners, so their uptime curves drift independently. A farm hosted on one server starts every clone at the same dawn reboot and drops them all in the same outage. If the ledger logs heartbeat times and pays any group with near-identical uptime as one seat, a grove of two hundred accounts shares a single reward, and a crash that sends them all to their nadir in the same second shows who planted them.
